title: Tuatha Dé Danann
extract: The Tuatha Dé Danann (Irish: Tuatha Dé Danann, meaning 'the folk of the goddess Danu') are the supernatural race of pre-Christian Irish mythology, often interpreted as the gods of the Gaelic world. They are described in the Lebor Gabála Érenn (Book of Invasions) as having inhabited Ireland before the arrival of the Milesians. They came to Ireland in dark clouds from four northern cities: Falias, Gorias, Finias, and Murias. The Tuatha Dé Danann fought two epic battles against the Fomorians at Mag Tuired, the Second Battle of Mag Tuired being the climactic battle in which they defeated the Fomorians and their high king Balor of the Evil Eye under the leadership of Lugh Lámhfhada. The Tuatha Dé Danann were eventually defeated by the Milesians and withdrew into the sídhe where they became the Aos Sí. The Trí Dé Dána are Brigid (poetry and healing), Dian Cecht (medicine), and Ogma (eloquence and learning). Cian, as Dian Cecht's son, is a member of this craftsman's lineage by direct descent.
